answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable bond before it may claim rewards. If several identities controlled by one attacker coordinate to double-claim or violate a rule, proof of the shared action lets the system confiscate their bonds. Creating Sybils is therefore not free: each one ties up capital, and detected abuse destroys it. The bond need not prove a person’s identity; it makes multiplying identities costly. A participant called oasis may keep a relic or sable, but neither name changes the same collateral requirement.
